_README: THE PROVENANCE CENSUS — one verdict per .tsx file that renders a figure.
Read by scripts/check_provenance_census.mjs, which discovers the sites
itself (17 figure primitives + 11 formatters + 3 natives, each verified
declared in its home on every run) and fails on anything unregistered,
stale, or count-drifted.
THE QUESTION EACH ENTRY ANSWERS: does the payload this file renders
actually carry provenance, and does the reader get the affordance?
HAS_SHOWS     payload carries it, affordance rendered. An entry with
affordances: 0 must name `renders_via` — the registered
HAS_SHOWS file whose primitive paints it (TC-7).
HAS_MISSING   payload (or its upstream) carries it, affordance NOT
rendered here — remaining work, NAMED in `why`
LACKS_SILENT  there is no origin to name, and nothing is claimed
LACKS_SHOWS   an affordance over a payload with nothing behind it.
The gate FAILS on this bucket; it is never a state to
sit in. Found live twice: CapsuleTier0Preview put the
PERIOD LABEL in the field the card labels Source
(2026-09-02); `?? 0` rows in ComprehensiveReport wore a
field path over a figure the envelope never carried
(2026-09-03). Both shapes are now antibodies in the gate.
UNAUDITED     nobody opened this file to decide. CEILING IS ZERO.
`sites` = primitive tags + formatter calls; `affordances` = opening tags
that RENDER the affordance, counted once each. Both are MEASURED, not
intentions. They drift the moment a figure is added or loses its
provenance, and the gate fails until someone re-states the verdict.
Re-derived 2026-09-04 from `node scripts/check_provenance_census.mjs
--dump`, after the five-tag census was found blind to 46 of these files.

frontend/components/cfo/AccountMenu.tsx.why: OPENED 2026-09-04. Two formatEur() on the plan price and three formatTokens() on this month's token usage. A plan price is a PRICE LIST entry and token usage is telemetry about the account; neither is read from a company's envelope, so there is no cell to name.

frontend/components/cfo/BSStatementView..why: Rows carry account_codes; the envelope carries extraction.sheet/method and mapping_version. Item rows get accounts+sheet+method+pack; aggregates get engine-subtotal+method+pack and deliberately NO sheet. KNOWN GAP: rows rendering a <LearnableNumber> (a button) are skipped to avoid nesting interactive elements.

frontend/components/cfo/BillingSection.t.why: OPENED 2026-09-04. formatEur() on plan prices from lib/plans.ts (a static price list). Not a company figure.

frontend/components/cfo/CashFlowStatemen.why: OPENED 2026-09-04. Indirect-method lines carry `accounts` (working-capital rows, capex items, 1621 for bank loans) and assembled_cf says whether it is approximated — an origin the reader could follow. EVERY amount renders inside <LearnableNumber> (a button), so wearing the affordance today nests one interactive element in another. Remaining work, named: lift the amount out of the button (the MetricCard stretched-sibling pattern) and wear {source: <filename> · assembled_cf.<field>, accounts, method: indirect method · approximated?}. Rendered plain until then.

frontend/components/cfo/CreditScoreCard..why: RE-MEASURED 2026-09-04 (one-composite lane): 12 -> 8. WHAT WENT: the four figure sites inside `variant="compact"`, a branch with ZERO callers that had been enumerated as the dashboard's live hero. The dashboard hero is `HeroVerdictCard` (frontend/pages/cfo/FinancialStatements.tsx), a projection of `computeCreditScore` in a different file; the only caller of this component is `ComprehensiveReport.tsx:480`, and it passes `variant="full"`. Counting an unmounted branch as a live surface inflated this file's provenance debt and, worse, credited it with coverage no rendered gate could reach. The branch is deleted. PRIOR ENTRY (kept, still true): composite / grade / Altman Z″ are server-computed in stage_compute and served as assembled_metrics.credit.* — the field path IS the origin, and FinancialStatements already names assembled_metrics.credit.composite_score for the hero score. Here the three headline figures sit inside <LearnableNumber> (a button) and the X1–X4 components are plain spans. Remaining work, named: reuse the hero's origin object on the X1–X4 spans and lift the headline out of the button. Rendered plain until then.

frontend/components/cfo/CurrentPlanCard..why: OPENED 2026-09-04. One formatEur() on the subscriber's own plan price. Not a company figure.

frontend/components/cfo/DatasetsPanel.ts.why: OPENED 2026-09-04. sku_count / row_count are the inventory of a dataset (how many rows it holds) — a count of the file, not a figure read from it. Nothing claimed.

frontend/components/cfo/EbitdaMultiplePr.why: OPENED 2026-09-04. EV, equity, low/high are client arithmetic over the multiple the reader drags — no cell, nothing to claim. But Core EBITDA and net debt are canonical metrics (the reconciliation panel beside it names their 758/781 line items) and both render inside <LearnableNumber> (a button). Remaining work, named: wear the canonical metric's origin on the plain restatements at the foot of the card (`currency formatCanonicalFull(coreEbitda)`, net debt). Derived figures stay plain by law.

Remaining work, named: the builder hands each line a provenance {source: <filename> · lineItems, accounts: line.accounts, period} and the non-button cells wear it. frontend/components/comparison/MoneyAmou.why: A transparent wrapper: converts source→display currency and spreads ...rest into <Amount>, so a caller's `provenance` passes through untouched. It holds no payload of its own and must claim nothing.

frontend/components/comparison/VarianceT.why: OPENED 2026-09-03. Same row payload as KpiVarianceStrip. Upstream, the ComparisonDataset the page holds names the uploaded budget file (`label`, `source: upload|demo`, `updatedAt`) — a document-level origin for the BUDGET column only; the LAST-YEAR column may come from that dataset OR from the period picker (F6.1b), and the row cannot tell which, so LY must stay plain until the page disambiguates. frontend/components/dashboard/MetricCard.why: Reads provenance by concept from FigureProvenanceProvider (lib/figureProvenanceContext) and attaches it ONLY when the resolved value equals the value the page vouched for, to the cent. Headline money/days/count/score values wear it; derived ratios (resolver arithmetic), PercentLevel/CappedMultiple (no provenance prop) and every trend badge (a delta over a series) render plain. The value block lifts above the stretched learn-trigger only when it has something to say.

frontend/components/instrument/Amount.ts.why: THE INSTRUMENT. Delegates to ProvenanceAffordance when the payload has substance; falls back to a plain rounding tooltip (no data-provenance, no dotted rule) when it does not.

frontend/components/instrument/shell/Tru.why: difference: `servedFacts.difference() · assets − (equity + liabilities)` — the GATEWAY accessor the receipt reads, not the raw envelope property (the import-boundary gate refuses a label that claims a raw read) — plus extraction.method and the mapping pack (an aggregate over served totals; no sheet, like the BS subtotals). original_difference adds the receipt's content_hash as snapshot; applied_delta adds origin/model/prompt_version as method and applied_at as computedAt. Absent receipt → the two reconciliation rows do not render at all. The sheet's initial focus goes to its title so the first card opens only when a reader tabs to it.

frontend/components/instrument/shell/cap.why: OPENED 2026-09-04. One NarrativeText: the answer's prose sentence. The figures it cites are painted as FigureValue rows beside it (CapsuleFigures, HAS_SHOWS), which wear the affordance; decorating the same numeral inside the sentence would put two cards over one number.
Renders CapsuleFigures.FigureValue, which owns the affordance. Zero here is correct: a second one would be a second card over the same number.

Money and dimensionless both wear it now. CapsuleFactMeta has no sheet or account, so it names period + tool (method) + snapshot and claims NO source — the mislabel that put periodLabel under Source is fixed.
WAS the LACKS_SHOWS case: `{ source: fact.periodLabel }` on every fact. Now amountProvenanceFor(fact) for both branches, so the sheet and account codes it always had are what the reader sees.
Share-of-class is DERIVED, so it shows the row's accounts and period with a method naming the division and its denominator; the balance renders through FactTileValue, which carries its own.
The MONEY branch was bare while its percent sibling carried the affordance; money now wraps NarrativeText in the same one.

frontend/lib/financialValuation.ts.why: RE-MEASURED 2026-09-04 (one-letter/one-ladder lane): 4 -> 3. WHAT WENT, AND THE PRIOR ADJUDICATION OF IT WAS WRONG: `numOrNull(e.altman_z_score) ?? altman.score` on the engine path (listed above as "(5th, same line family)" and excused as "precedence between TWO ENGINE-EMITTED sources of the same figure, both engine truth; `altmanFromEngine` merges them"). It did NOT merge them: that row BYPASSED `altmanFromEngine` and preferred `assembled_metrics.credit.altman_z_score`, while `altmanFromEngine` — whose AltmanResult is the Risks tab's `altman-score` and the zone chip beside it — prefers `calculated_metrics`. Two engine-emitted inputs, two different precedences, one measure. Measured in the DOM on the real Scandia FY2025 envelope with the two emissions split (envelope 0.22, calculated_metrics 3.09): the panel's headline printed 3.09 under a SAFE zone chip while its own component row printed 0.22 reading "Distress zone — immediate action required" — one panel, one company, a safe chip beside a distress sentence. In production both fields come off the same engine row, so it was LATENT, which is why a corpus sweep could not see it. The row now reads `altman.score` and `altman.zone` from the one AltmanResult, so a precedence exists in exactly one place. THE 3 THAT REMAIN, unchanged and re-checked against the same envelope: (1) `numOrNull(weights.altman) ?? 0.30` — a WEIGHT is a constant of the model (the locked 30/20/15/10/10/10/5 ladder), not a figure read off this company's book; the contribution beside it uses `contributionOf`, which propagates the absent SUB-SCORE. (2) the FE-fallback `read` ternary (`altman.score === null || altman.zone === null ? null : ...`) — a lint-regex false positive: it IS the refusal, not a substitution. (3) :46 `s.supplementary.capex ?? s.incomeStatement.depreciationAmortization` — the documented maintenance-capex assumption (capex proxied by D&A) that Appendix A's DCF specifies; a stated modelling choice, and it substitutes a MEASURED figure rather than a 0. ALSO CHANGED IN THIS LANE, no new substitution: `rating`/`grade` moved from `e.letter_grade ?? null` to `engineLetterGrade(e, composite)`, which falls back to the engine's OWN `letter_grade_bands` — an envelope carrying the ladder but not the letter used to refuse a verdict it had everything to state. Measured before the fix on that same envelope with `subscores` deleted: all six non-Altman rows printed 0.00 and the sentence "<label> component: weak" under an UNCHANGED composite 24.4 / CC; with the altman_x* metrics deleted, four 0.0000 component rows printed under an unchanged total. `AltmanResult.score`/`.zone`, `CreditScoreResult.score`/`.rating`/`.grade` and every component `value`/`contribution`/`read` are now `| null`, and the FE-fallback composite REFUSES (no score, no rating, no grade) when any term is unmeasured rather than summing over the gap into a worse letter — measured on served_balanced.json, emptying `totals` used to move the verdict from 88.80/A to 52.30/B off identical statements. (4) :46 `s.supplementary.capex ?? s.incomeStatement.depreciationAmortization` — the documented maintenance-capex assumption (capex proxied by D&A) that Appendix A's DCF specifies; a stated modelling choice, not an absent leaf read as zero, and it substitutes a MEASURED figure rather than a 0. _README_ABSENT_LEAF: THE ABSENT-LEAF LINT — one verdict per BUILDER file that substitutes an
absent payload leaf and feeds a card-bearing surface.
The census above this is a census of RENDER SITES: it asks whether a site
records a verdict, never whether the number arriving there is real. Every
fabrication this lane was opened for happens UPSTREAM, in a builder, so
the value reaches the affordance as a finite number and all five of its
guards correctly wave it through. This section is the missing axis.
SCOPE is derived from the import graph, not hand-listed: the modules a
card-bearing component imports directly. A new builder enters scope on
its next run with no edit to the gate.
FILED_ZERO     checked against a real envelope; the zero is filed, or
no figure is painted from the field. Justified in `why`.
OPEN_DEFECT    PROVEN to fabricate against a real fixture. Carries an
`owner`. Counted against CEILING_OPEN_DEFECT, which only
ever falls.
UNADJUDICATED  nobody has run this file against a real envelope yet. A
verdict about the EVIDENCE, which is true, rather than
about the payload, which would be invented. Ceilinged,
and the ceiling only falls.
`substitutions` is MEASURED. A new absent-to-zero drifts the count and
fails the gate until someone decides which bucket it is in.
